# swarmops ws snapshot

Record a workspace's edits as a changeset on its head, which moves no ref.

The workspace keeps its head, its files and its edits. The same edits on the same head again write nothing and answer the same id; ws info names the latest.

## Syntax

```text
swarmops ws snapshot [OPTIONS]
```

## Required arguments

None.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--ws`

Syntax: `--ws <NAME>`.

The workspace, by its name in the store's registry (default: the one around the working directory).

### `--ws-path`

Syntax: `--ws-path <DIR>`.

The workspace's directory.

### `--status-after`

Syntax: `--status-after <STATUS_AFTER>`.
Default: `page`.

page: the first page of the status follows the result; none: it is left out. Values: `page`: The first page of the status; `none`: No status.

## Return information

`result` is a `WsSnapshotResp` (`swarmops schema WsSnapshotResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `snapshot` | `string or null` | no | The snapshot, readable by id from any process; omitted when there were no edits. |
| `status_after` | `WsStatus or null` | no | The status after the mutation; omitted when the request said `none`. |
| `written` | `SnapshotWrite` | yes | Whether this call wrote it. |

Envelope `op`: `ws_snapshot`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
